title: SSE atomic tool-call microbatching and structured sentinel markers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an SSE-side microbatch coalescer that preserves atomicity for tool/function calls and emits explicit structured sentinel markers (JSONL) so clients can safely rehydrate in reconnect scenarios. This ticket covers the server framing change, client-visible sentinel format, backward-compatible headers, and a best-effort idempotency model for duplicated microbatches.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits sentinel markers between microbatches using a stable JSONL envelope that includes sequence_window_id and microbatch_id
Tool/function-call frames remain atomic: a microbatch containing a function call cannot be split across sentinel boundaries
Reconnect resume can reliably detect last-processed microbatch using the sentinel metadata and optional client ack header
Default behavior is backward compatible: clients that ignore sentinel markers see unchanged SSE payloads
Performance regression <= 6% p50 token latency in the standard latency benchmark for 1k RPS workload
E2E tests for atomic toolcall replay, duplicate-suppression hints, and sentinel-parsing implemented and green
technical_notes: Introduce 'X-Redwood-SSE-Sentinel: application/jsonl+redwood' header on stream start to advertise support

Sentinel envelope format: single-line JSON token prefixed with '�SENT
' to ensure streaming-friendly boundary detection
Microbatch coalescer will attach microbatch_id (UUID), sequence_window_id (monotonic per session), and commit_pos (server token index) to each sentinel
Function-call atomicity: runtime will pin KV-cache and tool call payloads to the microbatch; if a microbatch exceeds max_bytes, it will backpressure upstream instead of splitting the microbatch
Resume semantics: client may send 'Last-Sentinel: <sequence_window_id>:<microbatch_id>' in rejoin request; server will attempt byte-offset resume or replay from last complete microbatch
Best-effort idempotency: server emits duplicate_hint with a checksum; clients should dedupe using (microbatch_id, checksum)
Backward compatibility: if client doesn't send 'Last-Sentinel', server falls back to legacy resume token flow (resume-token header)
Observability: add sentinel emission counters and microbatch-latency histogram in Console; tag traces with microbatch_id
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Define sentinel envelope and update runtime streamer to emit envelope on feature-flag (branch behind feature flag)
Phase 2: Implement microbatch pinning for function/tool calls and backpressure hook
Phase 3: Add resume header parsing and server-side best-effort replay logic
Phase 4: Expose telemetry; build e2e tests and compatibility tests against legacy clients
Phase 5: Gradual rollout with canary (10% sessions) -> 50% -> 100% after 2 days of stability checks
progress_updates: 2026-01-22: Spike complete. Validated sentinel single-line JSONL approach against streaming parsers in node/python clients. No parsing ambiguity observed in tests.

2026-01-26: Prototype microbatch coalescer implemented. Observed ~4% p50 latency impact under synthetic workload when feature-flag enabled. Optimization opportunities identified (avoid extra copy on envelope attach).
2026-01-30: API review with PM and DX. Agreed on header names and non-breaking default. PM requested explicit guidance in SDKs for how to ack sentinels when clients want stronger resume guarantees.
2026-02-02: First PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1248 implementing sentinel emission behind ff. Initial CI failing due to race in stream flush; debugging in progress.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Sentinel envelope could be misinterpreted by proxies that rewrite SSE frames. Mitigation: include sentinel header advertise and fall back to resume-token flow when tunnel/edge strips header
Risk: Large function-call payloads may cause microbatch to exceed size; Mitigation: runtime will enforce per-microbatch max_bytes and expose a configurable knob to app teams
Risk: Clients that cache by byte-offset may end up with duplicate application-visible function calls. Mitigation: duplicate_hint checksum and microbatch_id for client-side dedupe
testing_plan: Integration tests: simulated reconnect with partial microbatch arrival; assert atomic toolcall semantics
Compatibility matrix: legacy client (no sentinel), sentinel-aware client, and proxy behavior test
Load test: 1k RPS sustained for 1 hour with feature enabled; compare latency and error rates
Chaos test: intermittent connection drops and replays; validate no double-execution of tool calls under normal duplicate_hint handling
qa_notes: For QA, use the 'sentinel-enabled' runtime ff and the sentinel-test client in tools/stream-test-client
Verify that when connection re-establishes with Last-Sentinel header, server does not re-emit microbatches older than the specified microbatch_id (or emits with duplicate_hint=true)
rollout_plan: Canary: enable ff for 10% of sessions (edge selection) for 24h
Monitor: microbatch-emitted, microbatch-resume-fallback, toolcall-duplication-rate, p50/p95 latency
If metrics stable, increase to 50% for 48h then 100%
Communication: notify integrators and publish SDK guidance note before 50% phase
notes_for_design: Design should include a simple visual in Console showing microbatch boundaries and the last-sentinel seen per session
Add explanatory copy in SDK docs on how to use duplicate_hint and microbatch_id for deduplication
